original_test_intent: Validate persistent AMD OOB UMC address/command-parity error reporting through a correctly decoded CPER while proving the persistent condition can be deterministically stopped and the GPU/host returned to health.
original_method: Record topology, workload/health and complete CPER baseline; validate secure Systems/UBB Dump endpoint and mode2 stop semantics; prove device0/block0 mapping; run literal severity4/type4/mode2 once for the approved bounded window; select one attributable new entry, download/hash/transfer/decode its attachment and check OAM/UMC/ext4/type/fatal fields; execute owner-approved stop/clear without retry, monitor for no further CPER/error storm, recover GPU/BMC/host and preserve artifacts.
manual_activity: AMD/board owner supplies and controls mode2 lifetime, stop/clear and recovery; agent may baseline/query CPER, hash/decode the attributable attachment and monitor post-stop health.
required_inputs: Platform/UBB/BMC/host and all GPU UUID/OAM/BDF/firmware/driver topology
amdgpuras/cdump_analyzer versions/hashes/licenses and exact `-m2` arm/lifetime semantics
Authoritative stop/clear command, completion signal and no-error-storm observation window
Secure Systems/UBB Dump endpoint, credentials/CA, CPER schema and attribution rules
Dedicated no-workload window and GPU/BMC/host reset/recovery boundaries
safety_requirements: Dedicated SUT; no active GPU processes/jobs and live BMC/OOB recovery
Prove numeric target/block and persistent stop path before arming
One mode2 command only; bounded observation and hard abort
Stop immediately on error storm, unexpected reset/fatal state, loss of management or multiple ambiguous entries
Execute approved clear/recovery, preserve evidence and verify no continuing errors before any future case
agent_execution_scope: Validate target/tool/endpoint, baseline and stop plan
Observe one approved persistent window and retrieve/decode one attributable CPER
Do not arm/extend/retry/clear/reset independently or issue PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve target and mode2 lifetime/stop semantics
Define acceptable CPER production and quiet period

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run one bounded persistent UMC injection, decode its uniquely attributable CPER and prove deterministic termination plus recovered quiet health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds a preapproved lifecycle/abort, secure endpoint, collision-proof artifact provenance and post-stop monitoring.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The source criteria prove reporting but not that a persistent injector stopped; both are required for safe readiness.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Mode2 can emit repeated fatal errors, reset the GPU/host or overwhelm logs; without a verified stop path it must not be executed.

project_override_considerations: The example HTTP address and resource require canonical project mapping. The source omits stop/clear mechanics; this remains an engineering prerequisite rather than guessed implementation or an automatic BLOCKED classification.

Stop/clear result, no-new-CPER/error-storm quiet window and recovered GPU/BMC/host health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently requests persistent mode2 and the same CPER fields as the single-shot variant; its missing termination procedure is an explicit prerequisite, not a contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The persistent lifecycle and recovery are known missing vendor/operator inputs that can be supplied; the purpose, stimulus and acceptance remain identifiable.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row180 Wistron-GPU RAS-00467-V004: approve platform/UBB/BMC/host and device0 UUID/OAM/BDF plus block0=UMC mapping; provide amdgpuras/cdump_analyzer versions/hashes/licenses, exact `-s4 -t4 -m2` arm/duration semantics and stop/clear command, canonical secure Systems/UBB Dump endpoint and CPER attribution/decoder schema, allowed CPER rate/quiet window, and GPU/BMC/host OOB no-retry recovery.

review_improvement: Separates persistent lifecycle safety from single-shot reporting, preserves full CPER attachment decoding and prevents leaving a fatal injector active after a superficially correct CPER.
independent_technical_reasoning: Mode2 is not merely a different command flag: the error source may remain armed and repeatedly exercise the fatal UMC path. Therefore one matching CPER establishes reporting but not safe completion. The run must have an approved stop before start, identify an attributable CPER despite possible multiple entries, then demonstrate a quiet period and recovered device state. A retry would multiply fatal events and destroy causal attribution.
